text: There is a jellyfish people call immortal. Is that true?
Meet Turritopsis dohrnii. Smaller than your fingernail.
Most jellyfish grow up, reproduce, and die.
When it's injured, starving, or stressed, the adult sinks and turns back into a polyp, its baby stage.
In the lab, scientists watched it cycle back and forth, again and again.
So it doesn't have to die of old age.
It can still be eaten. By fish, sea turtles, even other jellyfish. And it can die from disease.
As one researcher put it: if they were truly immortal, the ocean would be full of them.
Verdict: half true. It can beat old age, not everything else.
Now scientists study its genes to understand aging itself.
